recipes.title: Query a Postgres table and validate a result
recipes.body:
Connects via the shared PostgresHelper and runs a parameterized query.

```java
var row = PostgresHelper.queryOne(conn, sql, id);
```

recipes.title: Query a Postgres table and validate a result (Python)
recipes.body:
Connects via the shared postgres_helper module and runs a parameterized query.

```python
row = postgres_helper.query_one(conn, sql, params)
```

recipes.title: Connection helper
recipes.body:
Opens a session and runs a CQL query against the configured keyspace.

```java
var row = ConnectionHelper.queryOne(session, cql, id);
```

recipes.title: Query a MySQL table
recipes.body:
Connects via the shared MysqlHelper and executes a query.

```java
var row = MysqlHelper.queryOne(conn, sql, id);
```

recipes.title: Publish a Kafka event
recipes.body:
Publishes a message to the configured topic and waits for the send to complete.

```java
KafkaProducerHelper.publish(topic, key, payload);
```

recipes.title: Take a screenshot and save it to disk
recipes.body:
Captures the current page and writes it to the given path.

```python
take_screenshot(page, "out.png")
```

recipes.title: Attach a bearer auth token to an API request
recipes.body:
Fetches a fresh bearer token and attaches it to the request's Authorization header.

```java
AuthTokenHelper.attachBearerToken(request);
```

recipes.title: Assert an API response's status code and body shape
recipes.body:
Validates the response status code and that the body matches the expected shape.

```java
ApiAssertions.assertSuccessful(response);
```

recipes.title: Validate an API response is successful
recipes.body:
An alternative helper that checks a response is a 2xx with a non-empty body.

```java
ResponseValidator.validateOk(response);
```

queries.queryText: Login to Postgres database, query a specific table using a query, validate the result
queries.rationale: Direct, near-exact wording match against the postgres-query-one recipe's own title/tags.

queries.queryText: open a database connection and run a query against the orders table to check the returned value
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of dev-positive-exact — no exact phrase overlap ('open'/'orders' not in the recipe), tests semantic/lexical robustness beyond literal string matching.

queries.queryText: use PostgresHelper.queryOne to fetch a row from the accounts table for validation
queries.rationale: References the recipe's own compound identifier (PostgresHelper.queryOne) directly — tests camelCase/identifier-splitting tokenization (tfidfEmbeddings.ts's extractFeatures).

queries.queryText: Login to Postgres database, query a specific table using a query, validate the result
queries.rationale: Identical wording to dev-positive-exact but language=python — the JAVA-only postgres-query-one must be excluded by the hard language filter; only the Python twin should surface.

queries.queryText: connect to a mysql database and execute a query to check a row
queries.rationale: Vendor-specific wording (mysql) among multiple same-shaped database helpers (postgres, mysql, cassandra) — tests that vendor names are never conflated/canonicalized onto each other.

queries.queryText: Verify all the details validated on the UI page are also validated in this cassandra table, write a query to validate the table
queries.rationale: Real-world regression case from this project's own bug history: shares generic vocabulary ('database', 'query', 'validate') with postgres/mysql recipes, but the word 'cassandra' only appears in the target recipe's FOLDER name, not its title/tags/body — must still rank first via folder-name matching, not get outranked by the shared-vocabulary noise.

queries.queryText: connect to postgres to fetch the order data, then publish a kafka event with the result

operations.text: connect to postgres to fetch the order data
publish a kafka event with the result

queries.rationale: Two DIFFERENT required capabilities in one request. The LEGACY/BASELINE benchmark mode (runBenchmarkOnDataset(), F15) deliberately ignores `operations` and scores this as a single whole-query retrieval call with topK=2 — real, expected recall<1 there. The PRODUCTION-PIPELINE mode (runProductionPipelineOnDataset()) DOES use `operations` for real per-operation retrieval, exactly like the actual application (Phase 3) — this case is exactly what distinguishes the two modes from each other.

queries.queryText: query postgres for the customer row, then query postgres again for the linked order row

operations.text: query postgres for the customer row
query postgres again for the linked order row

queries.rationale: The SAME capability needed twice — only one distinct helper is required, not two. `operations` here is used by the PRODUCTION-PIPELINE benchmark mode (runProductionPipelineOnDataset(), Phase 3's real per-operation retrieval) but deliberately ignored by the LEGACY/BASELINE mode (runBenchmarkOnDataset()), which always scores this as one whole-query call regardless.
A whitespace-only query must return zero matches without erroring — retrieveRagMatches() already special-cases this.

queries.queryText: generate a random UUID value for use as a unique test identifier
queries.rationale: Deliberate no-match case — nothing in the corpus concerns UUID generation. (Earlier wording accidentally shared 'debugging' with screenshot-helper's own tags and produced a real false positive here — the benchmark itself caught that dataset-authoring mistake, which is exactly what it's for.)

queries.queryText: query the cassandra keyspace to validate a stored value
queries.rationale: Held-out positive case for the same cassandra folder-matching capability as dev-misleading-shared-vocab-cassandra, with different wording, kept in a separate split to avoid leakage.

queries.queryText: add a bearer token to the request before calling the API
queries.rationale: Held-out positive case for the API auth-token helper.

queries.queryText: call the API and check the response came back successfully
queries.rationale: Either of the two near-duplicate API-response-checking helpers satisfies this request — an alternative-helper group, not two independently required capabilities.

queries.queryText: python script that talks to postgres and fetches rows for validation
queries.rationale: Held-out Python-language positive case, distinct wording from dev-language-incompatibility.

queries.queryText: resize the browser window to a custom viewport size before starting the test
queries.rationale: Deliberate no-match case in the holdout split — nothing in the corpus concerns viewport/window sizing.
